ratings.source: Google Maps rating and review count

demand.source: Google Trends, Rajasthan (index within each query set)

findings.headline: of all Google reviews go to one café in ten.
findings.body: The typical café has 82 reviews; 54% have fewer than a hundred. Most cafés compete in a long tail, where every review moves them further.
how: We sorted the 410 cafés with Google reviews from most reviewed to least and added up the top tenth.
Resampling the cafés 2,000 times puts the share between 63% and 74% (95% interval).
The Gini coefficient, a 0-to-1 measure of how unevenly something is shared, is 0.80. Zero would mean every café had the same number of reviews.

findings.headline: of cafés have ten or more others within a five-minute walk.
findings.body: The typical café has 42 neighbours within 500 metres. Cafés sit closer together than chance would put them: 28% in C-Scheme, 40% in Malviya Nagar.
how: For each of the 464 mapped cafés we counted the others within 500 metres, about a five-minute walk.
To test for clustering we compared the average distance to the nearest café with what the same number of cafés, scattered at random over the same ground, would give (the Clark-Evans test).
C-Scheme: 56 m observed against 78 m at random; Malviya Nagar: 90 m observed against 150 m at random. Gaps this large would arise by chance less than one time in a hundred.

findings.headline: of cafés with under ten reviews rate 4.8 or more.
findings.body: Past a thousand reviews, 4% do. A high score on a handful of reviews is mostly luck; it settles as the reviews arrive. Read a new café's rating with its review count beside it.
how: We grouped the 398 rated cafés by how many reviews they have and took the share rated 4.8 or above in each group.
Ratings also spread less as reviews grow: the typical gap from the group average falls from 0.55 stars to 0.24.

Across all cafés, more reviews go with a lower rating (rank correlation -0.37; a shuffle test puts the chance of this by luck below 0.001). This is regression to the mean, not a sign that popular cafés are worse.

findings.headline: of cafés score higher on Google than on Zomato.
findings.body: The same café averages 0.38 stars more on Google. Compare a café with others on the same platform, never across platforms.
how: We took the 102 cafés rated on both Google and Zomato dine-in and subtracted one rating from the other, café by café.
Resampling those cafés 4,000 times puts the average gap between 0.28 and 0.47 stars (95% interval), clear of zero.
11% score the same on both; 19% score higher on Zomato.

findings.headline: of Zomato cafés have more delivery reviews than dine-in.
findings.body: 74% have at least one delivery review. For most cafés the packed order is reviewed more often than the table.
how: For the 211 cafés listed on Zomato we compared each café's count of delivery reviews with its dine-in reviews.
The share is between 51% and 64% (95% Wilson interval).

findings.headline: more reviews for cafés that list Wi-Fi, at first glance.
findings.body: Cafés with Wi-Fi also tend to be bigger, list more of everything (3.9 other features against 2.3) and price higher. Holding area, type and price level, the Wi-Fi gap is +35%, too uncertain to call. The listing that still stands out is kid-friendly.
how: Raw gap: the median Google reviews of cafés that list a feature against those that don't, for the 151 cafés on Zomato with a listed price.
Like for like: a regression on the logarithm of reviews that holds area, café type and price level fixed, so each feature is compared against cafés that are otherwise similar.
Bars show a 90% interval from 3,000 resamples. An interval crossing zero means the data can't tell the effect from none.
This is association, not cause: a listing can mark the kind of café that draws reviews without drawing them itself.

findings.headline: of cafés charge ₹500 or less for two.
findings.body: The typical café charges ₹600 for two: ₹700 in C-Scheme and ₹500 in Malviya Nagar. Price tells you nothing about the rating: dearer cafés rate no higher.
how: Cost for two as listed on Zomato, for 193 cafés.
Price against Google rating, for 150 cafés: rank correlation -0.01, where zero means no link and ±1 a perfect one. A shuffle test finds nothing (chance of a link this size by luck: 0.89).
Price does go with more reviews, weakly; dearer cafés tend to be bigger.

findings.headline: of cafés list five or more cuisines.
findings.body: The typical menu spans 7. Fast food is listed by 63% of cafés, coffee by 49%. Jaipur's cafés are small restaurants first; a short, focused menu is the rarer position.
how: The cuisine tags each of 211 cafés lists on Zomato. 'Café' and 'Beverages', which nearly all list, are left out of the chart.

findings.headline: of cafés turn up on only one platform.
findings.body: 80% on Google Maps; 41% on Zomato; 20% on Swiggy. A café missing from Zomato or Swiggy is missing from the place many people choose where to go.
how: Each of the 511 cafés matched across the platform searches we run every two weeks.
Absent means it did not appear in our searches of that platform, which is how a customer browsing the area would miss it too.

findings.headline: of Malviya Nagar's cafés are chai cafés.
findings.body: In C-Scheme it is 8%, where coffee-led cafés are a larger share (33% against 25%). A lean, not yet a firm difference: the gap could still be chance.
how: The type mix of all 511 operating cafés, by area.
A chi-square test, run by shuffling the area labels 2,000 times, puts the chance of a mix this different by luck at 0.06.

profiles.name: Town Coffee
profiles.tagline: The coffee house Jaipur works from.

story.text: Built for staying: fast Wi-Fi and a room full of laptops made the Malviya Nagar café, near World Trade Park, a go-to for people who work remotely.

source.title: Town Coffee in Jaipur: Perfect Cafe for Digital Nomads

story.text: A menu that goes beyond the cup, with mezze platters, sandwiches and baked pasta alongside coffee and cold drinks: somewhere you can stay for lunch, not just a latte.

source.title: Town Coffee in Jaipur: Perfect Cafe for Digital Nomads

story.text: The format has travelled: Town Coffee now appears in both areas we track, Malviya Nagar and C-Scheme.
